# LiFePO4 vs NMC: LiFePO4 is better for most people

**Cycle life is the biggest difference.** LiFePO4 (LFP) stations are typically rated for 3,000 to 6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500 to 800 for older NMC units. At one full cycle a day, that is about 8 to 11 years versus under 2 years ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Check the percentage in the rating, though. "3,000 cycles to 70%" promises less than "to 80%."

**Safety:** LFP fails more mildly. In lab tests on small cells, an NMC cell peaked at 731°C versus 259°C for LFP ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Another study found NMC cells ignited, while LFP released smoke without flames. But LFP isn't fireproof. One test found it reached thermal runaway earlier under overcharge ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).

**Weight:** NMC cells are denser, but the gap mostly disappears in finished stations. The median NMC model in one database holds only about 10% more Wh per pound than the median LFP model ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). One LFP station (Anker SOLIX C1000) is lighter per Wh than an NMC Goal Zero Yeti 1000.

**Cost:** LFP has caught up. One retailer database shows a median of $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Cold weather:** Don't treat this as a differentiator. Some guides claim LFP handles cold better, but the manuals checked show both chemistries refusing to charge below 32°F ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Check your specific model's manual.

## When NMC makes sense
Only if you carry the unit often, use it rarely, and weight matters. If you already own a working NMC unit, keep using it.

## Examples you can buy
These are affiliate links, so Dealectric is paid if you buy. Prices were checked Oct 21 to 24, 2026 and may change.

- **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (LiFePO4):** 2,073.6 Wh, 6,000+ cycles to 80%, $899 ($854.05 with code AFF5OFF). Heavy at 24.2 kg. [Buy](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)
- **BLUETTI AC180 (LiFePO4):** 1,152 Wh, 3,500+ cycles, $499 ($474.05 with AFF5OFF). The $499 price is for the station alone. [Buy](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)
- **ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro (NMC):** 1,451 Wh, 2,400 W, about 13 kg, 2,500+ cycles, $664 ($597.60 with EXTRA10 until Nov 15). Worth it only if weight is your priority. [Buy](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-s2000-pro-1451wh)

Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/portable-power-station-lifepo4-nmc-battery-chemistry-manufacturer-comparison-202). That page notes the S2000 Pro's solar input and the P1800's cycle and UPS specs are listed inconsistently by the maker.
